extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2-million-example open supervised fine-tuning (SFT) dataset for training reasoning models across math (850,000), code (250,000), and science (100,000) domains, generated using QwQ-32B as a teacher model.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smyrnis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvarna, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were sourced across code, math, and science domains from existing datasets, online forums, and textbooks. The pipeline filtered the questions, applied deduplication, randomly sampled subsets to achieve the target domain mixture (850k math, 250k code, 100k science), and sampled 16 answers per question from teacher models.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: OpenMath-2-Math for math questions; StackExchange CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code questions; StackExchange Physics and Organic Chemistry PDF Pipeline (extracted from textbooks and SCP-116k) for science questions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Difficulty-based filtering using GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response-length filtering using GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions. Sampling 16 answers per question using teacher model QwQ-32B.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Exact deduplication based on Normalized Indel similarity for math and science questions, and no deduplication for code. Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using Normalized Indel similarity (75% threshold) and 13-gram overlap.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers containing step-by-step thinking tokens and final solutions were generated synthetically using QwQ-32B via 16x repeated sampling per question without answer filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Extensive ablations across verification and answer filtering techniques (including majority consensus, GPT verification, FastText classifiers, and length-based selection) revealed that answer filtering did not outperform retaining all generated answers, leading to the decision to omit answer filtering in the final pipeline.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen/QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Supervised fine-tuning on reasoning datasets inadvertently degrades pre-existing safety alignment, as observed by increased harmfulness rates on Harmbench and elevated over-refusal rates on XSTEST, highlighting a trade-off between reasoning performance and model safety.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not explore reinforcement learning data regimes, staged SFT, or curriculum learning. Distilled models trained on this data exhibit generalization deficits on structure-preserving task variations (such as Alice in Wonderland problems) and diminished safety alignment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for training open-source reasoning large language models across math, science, and coding tasks.
